Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:36747
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 9905 of 2024

Appellant :- Rahim Khan
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Diwakar Tiwari,Gyanendra Singh,Shobhit Yadav
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
(Ref:- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 1 of 2024)
1.

This Criminal appeal under Section 14A (2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant Rahim Khan with the prayer to set aside the
impugned judgement and order dated 04.09.2024 passed by learned Special Judge Sc/St
Act/Additional Sessions Judge, Banda rejecting the bail application of the appellant and to release
the appellant in Case Crime No. 135 of 2024, under Section 376 I.P.C. and Section 3 (2) 5 of
S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Pailani, District Banda.
2. Heard learned Counsel for the appellant-applicant as well as the learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The prosecution story in brief is that F.I.R. of this case was lodged by the informant, husband of the victim, alleging therein that the accused Sarwari, Asgari, Istakhar Khan and Ali Hussain alongwith the appellant Rahim Khan kidnapped his wife and some jewellery and cash were also taken from his wife.
The incident occurred on 23.06.2024 at about 10.00 A.M.

However, F.I.R. was Rahim Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26578995/
1 lodged on 26.06.2024 under Section 365 I.P.C.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After investigation, Section 365 I.P.C. was deleted and charge sheet under section 376 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)V SC/ST Act was submitted.
4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant-applicant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the victim lady of this case is a married lady and it is alleged that she was kidnapped by the accused persons named in the F.I.R.
However, from perusal of the statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. made by the victim herself it does not transpire that she was kidnapped by the appellant.

In the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has stated that she had left her house for Pailani Dera and accused Sarwari asked her to go to Kanpur where she met with the appellant Rahim Khan who took her away to his room and committed rape upon her.
Subsequently she informed her husband who came to Kanpur to take his wife.

It is next submitted that contradictory statements have been made by the victim herself under Section 164 Cr.P.C. where she made an improvement in the prosecution story and alleged that obscene photographs were sent in her mobile phone.
It is next submitted that the accused persons were trying for conversion of her religion.
It is next submitted that the evidence rendered by the prosecution regarding recovery of mobile phone is a concocted story.
It is next submitted that the appellant is languishing in jail since 31.07.2024 having no criminal history to his credit.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

5. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail application and it has been submitted that the victim lady was kidnapped by the accused persons named in the F.I.R. and subsequently rape was committed upon her by blackmailing her by way of some obscene photographs.
It is further submitted that the victim has corroborated the prosecution story.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned judgment.

7. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, taking into account the contents of the mobile phone of the victim prima facie was not proved in lawful manner as electronic evidence and also contradictory statements made by the victim herself in the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., and also taking into account that the victim lady had left her house herself, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The court concerned erred in rejecting the bail application of the appellant.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.
8. Accordingly, the bail application and appeal are allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

9. Let the appellant Rahim Khan involved in Case Crime No. 135 of 2024, under Section 376 I.P.C.
and Section 3 (2) 5 of S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Pailani, District Banda be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.

sentences.text: (i). The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii).
The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv). The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v). The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
